destination.name: Jervis Bay
destination.tagline: White-sand beaches, dolphins and a national park on a protected bay.
destination.description: Jervis Bay is described by Wikivoyage as one of the most beautiful parts of the NSW South Coast and an extremely popular summer destination. Hyams Beach is known for fine, squeaky quartz sand, and Booderee National Park covers most of the Jervis Bay Territory, which is administered separately from New South Wales. Huskisson is the largest town and the base for cruises that watch dolphins, and whales from June to November.

goodToKnow.title: Booderee has its own fee
goodToKnow.detail: Booderee is in the Jervis Bay Territory, so it charges a separate entry fee (about $20 per the brief) and NSW national park passes are not valid there.

goodToKnow.title: Book ahead for summer
goodToKnow.detail: Wikivoyage warns accommodation can be fully booked months before Christmas and New Year, and the bay is very busy at peak times.

goodToKnow.title: Beecroft opens at set times
goodToKnow.detail: Beecroft Peninsula is a military range open Fri 12:00 PM – 6:00 PM, weekends to 6:00 PM, and school and most public holidays; the lighthouse is at the end of a gravel road.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} are the warm swimming months, though Christmas and New Year are the busiest weeks.
